cards.title: Today’s vocabulary
sections: check in · /tʃɛk ˈɪn/ · verb · Phrase · New
tell a hotel that you have arrived. Can I check in now?
room key · /ˈrum ki/ · noun · Phrase · New
a key or card that opens a hotel room. Puck checks in and gets his room key.
A person whose job is to welcome and help visitors at a front desk. The receptionist asks for my name.
a plastic card used instead of a metal key to open a door. Use your keycard to open the hotel room.
at the front desk · /æt ðə frʌnt dɛsk/ · phrase · Phrase · New
At the place where visitors speak to staff when they arrive. We ask for our room key at the front desk.

cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 115 - Pronunciation & Listening - 01

articulation.label: check in
articulation.alt: check in: /tʃ/ → /ɛ/ → /k/ → /ɪ/ → /n/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /tʃ/: Brief closure, then a narrow sh-like release.
/ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/k/: Back of tongue meets the soft palate; release.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/n/: Tip at the ridge; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
